comments.note: TarXzArchiveExtractor.cs contains a well-documented TODO comment (lines 22-37) noting missing audit logging for extraction events. The class doc references Security Auditor finding A09. This is already tracked in-source and out of scope for this WP.

FfmpegProvisioner.EnsureAsync creates targetDir unconditionally (Directory.CreateDirectory) before extraction, so an empty target directory is left on disk if extraction is cancelled mid-way. The comment at step 8 acknowledges this. A guard or cleanup in the catch block would eliminate the leftover empty directory.

comments.note: EnsureAsync Enabled=false branch (FfmpegProvisioner.cs ~L73-78) returns BuildToolPathsFromOptions without validating that FfprobePath/FfmpegPath are non-empty or that the files exist on disk. This is intentional by design — the caller bears responsibility for ensuring valid paths when disabling auto-provisioning — but is worth documenting explicitly to avoid operator confusion.

No additional edge-case failures found. The Enabled=false test correctly uses Unix-style paths (/usr/bin/ffprobe) which do not exist on Windows, confirming the short-circuit bypass of File.Exists is working as intended.

summary: Reviewed new test EnsureAsync_ProvisioningDisabled_ShortCircuitsAndReturnsCachedPaths and independently verified all D-1/D-2/D-7/D-8 source claims. All correct — no blocking issues found.

New test correctly covers Enabled=false short-circuit: uses Unix paths that cannot pass File.Exists, asserts downloader.CallCount==0 and extractor.CallCount==0, and verifies returned ToolPaths mirrors the persisted FfprobePath/FfmpegPath/ResolvedVersion. Test follows all file conventions exactly.
D-1 confirmed: IsCacheHitAsync is private static Task<bool> with four Task.FromResult returns and no blocking calls (FfmpegProvisioner.cs ~L232-260).
D-2 confirmed: both FfprobePath and FfmpegPath are guarded with string.IsNullOrEmpty + File.Exists before returning Task.FromResult(true).
D-7 confirmed: Manifest property initializer in FfmpegProvisioningOptions.cs line 45 uses new Dictionary<string, ToolManifestEntry>() — mutable type, allows JSON deserialization.
D-8 confirmed: SymbolicLink/HardLink rejection (throw InvalidDataException) in TarXzArchiveExtractor.cs is placed before normalizedName computation and path-traversal guard — correct ordering.

comments.note: EnsureAsync_ProvisioningDisabled_ShortCircuitsAndReturnsCachedPaths defines a local const string cachedVersion = "n7.1" that duplicates the class-level TestVersion constant (same value). The local constant is benign and arguably makes the test self-contained, but if TestVersion ever changes the local const would silently diverge. Not a blocker — left as an observation for future test maintenance.

[documentation-forward] FfmpegProvisioner.EnsureAsync step-1 short-circuit (lines ~73-78) returns BuildToolPathsFromOptions without validating that FfprobePath/FfmpegPath are non-empty or that the files exist on disk. This is intentional by design (caller bears responsibility when disabling auto-provisioning), but there is no inline comment saying so. Add a /// <remarks> or inline comment to the Enabled=false branch noting that path validation is the caller's responsibility in this mode, to prevent future operator confusion and to document the deliberate design decision.
No other issues found. Code is clean, well-structured, and consistent with project conventions. All acceptance criteria are accurately met as verified by source inspection.
